---
title: GitHub as a Project Management Tool
subtitle: Plan, conduct, document, and share a master's thesis with one repository and one Project
description: Workshop and open educational resource, in the browser or on the command line. University of Bern, Digital Humanities, HS2026.
---

This workshop shows how to manage a master's thesis with GitHub. You work on a **fictional thesis** with **synthetic data**. Each exercise runs in the browser, where you install nothing, or on the command line with git and gh. You choose the route, and you can change it at any step.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
- **When:** Friday, 16 October 2026, 09:00–13:00
- **Where:** Seminarraum F 001, Hörraumgebäude Unitobler
- **Credits:** 0.5 ECTS, passed or failed
- **You need:** a laptop, a current browser, and a GitHub account. For the command-line route, also git and gh ([Setup](course/setup.qmd#command-line-route))
- **Course catalogue:** [KSL 526141, HS2026](https://www.ksl.unibe.ch/KSL/kurzansicht?stammNr=526141&semester=HS2026&lfdNr=0)
:::

## The workshop in one look

The core exercises X1–X4 build one complete workflow: a repository, Issues, a Project, and a pull request. Each exercise adds one step to the same thesis plan. Two optional extensions build on the core when you need them. The workshop teaches less, so that you can use what it teaches.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    A["<b>X1 Repository</b><br/>09:15 · a home for files and history"] --> B["<b>X2 Requirements → Issues</b><br/>09:45 · each task has a reason and a proof"]
    B --> C["<b>X3 Project</b><br/>10:35 · backlog, board, roadmap, milestones"]
    C --> D["<b>X4 Pull request</b><br/>11:20 · do the work, review it, close the Issue"]
    D -.-> E["<b>X5 Release</b><br/>optional · decide what to publish"]
    D -.-> F["<b>X6 Re-plan</b><br/>optional · react to a delay, record the decision"]
    F -.-> C
```

## How to use this site

1. **New to GitHub?** Read the [cheat sheet](course/cheat-sheet.qmd) first. It explains repositories, Issues, pull requests, and the other terms of the workshop.
2. Prepare with [Setup](course/setup.qmd). Create a GitHub account and choose a path: solo, private, or pair.
3. Read the [Syllabus](course/syllabus.qmd) for the aims, the run of show, and the pass rule. The [approaches](course/approaches.qmd) page covers the project-management background.
4. Work through the core exercises X1–X4 in order. Each exercise page has the same parts: why, steps, screenshots, expected state, and what to do if something goes wrong. Steps that start with **Optional:** can wait.
5. Use the [slides](slides/index.qmd) for an overview of the whole session.
6. After the session, move to your real thesis and keep the plan up to date: [After the workshop](course/after.qmd). Do the optional extensions X5 and X6 when your thesis needs them.

## Exercises

The core exercises fill the session. Nobody needs to complete an exercise to pass.

| Core exercise | Time | You produce |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [X1 Create the repository](course/exercises/x1.qmd) | 09:15–09:45 | Repository from the template, README, visibility check |
| [X2 Turn requirements into work](course/exercises/x2.qmd) | 09:45–10:25 | 2 epics, 6 sub-issues, 1 user story |
| [X3 Configure the Project](course/exercises/x3.qmd) | 10:35–11:20 | Project with 3 views, 3 milestones, 1 dependency |
| [X4 Complete one documentation task](course/exercises/x4.qmd) | 11:20–12:00 | Branch, pull request, review, merge, closed Issue |

| Optional extension | Time | You produce |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [X5 Prepare a reusable output](course/exercises/x5.qmd) | Self-paced, about 35 minutes | Data dictionary, citation check, demo release |
| [X6 React to a delay and a restriction](course/exercises/x6.qmd) | Self-paced, about 25 minutes | Re-plan, decision record, exported view |

## The worked example

The [showcase Project](https://github.com/users/maehr/projects/11) holds the full plan of the fictional thesis: eight epics, 34 sub-issues, three milestones, dependencies, and the views Backlog, Board, and Roadmap. Its Issues live in the [example repository](https://github.com/maehr/projm-example-thesis). Compare your work with it, or copy the Project as a starting point. The [Worked example](documentation/index.qmd) page shows its views and what each part holds.

## What this course is, and what it is not

- It is an **open educational resource** and a **worked documentation example**. See [Worked example](documentation/index.qmd).
- It is **not** a thesis-format template that the university approved. Your study plan, your supervisor, and the Dean's Office set the rules for your thesis. The [requirements register](documentation/requirements.qmd) shows how to keep the two apart.
- It does **not** use real personal or research data. For your real thesis, start **private**: see [Transfer to a private thesis](course/after.qmd#private-thesis).
